standards.description: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences.
standards.ccssText: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

standards.description: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text; summarize the text.
standards.ccssText: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text; summarize the text.

standards.description: Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text.
standards.ccssText: Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (e.g., a character's thoughts, words, or actions).

standards.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including those that allude to significant characters found in mythology.
standards.ccssText: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including those that allude to significant characters found in mythology (e.g., Herculean).

standards.description: Explain major differences between poems, drama, and prose, and refer to the structural elements of poems and drama when writing or speaking about a text.
standards.ccssText: Explain major differences between poems, drama, and prose, and refer to the structural elements of poems (e.g., verse, rhythm, meter) and drama (e.g., casts of characters, settings, descriptions, dialogue, stage directions) when writing or speaking about a text.

standards.description: Compare and contrast the point of view from which different stories are narrated, including the difference between first- and third-person narrations.
standards.ccssText: Compare and contrast the point of view from which different stories are narrated, including the difference between first- and third-person narrations.

standards.skillName: Make connections between text and visual
standards.description: Make connections between the text of a story or drama and a visual or oral presentation of the text, identifying where each version reflects specific descriptions and directions in the text.
standards.ccssText: Make connections between the text of a story or drama and a visual or oral presentation of the text, identifying where each version reflects specific descriptions and directions in the text.

standards.description: Compare and contrast the treatment of similar themes and topics and patterns of events in stories, myths, and traditional literature from different cultures.
standards.ccssText: Compare and contrast the treatment of similar themes and topics (e.g., opposition of good and evil) and patterns of events (e.g., the quest) in stories, myths, and traditional literature from different cultures.

clusters.name: Range of reading and level of text complexity

standards.description: By end of year, read and comprehend literature at the high end of the grades 4-5 text complexity band independently and proficiently.
standards.ccssText: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, in the grades 4–5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

standards.description: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences.
standards.ccssText: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

standards.description: Determine the main idea of a text and explain how it is supported by key details; summarize the text.
standards.ccssText: Determine the main idea of a text and explain how it is supported by key details; summarize the text.

standards.description: Explain events, procedures, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text, including what happened and why, based on specific information in the text.
standards.ccssText: Explain events, procedures, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text, including what happened and why, based on specific information in the text.

standards.description: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words or phrases in a grade 4 informational text.
standards.ccssText: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words or phrases in a text relevant to a grade 4 topic or subject area.

standards.description: Describe the overall structure of events, ideas, concepts, or information in a text or part of a text.
standards.ccssText: Describe the overall structure (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in a text or part of a text.

standards.description: Compare and contrast a firsthand and secondhand account of the same event or topic; describe the differences in focus and the information provided.
standards.ccssText: Compare and contrast a firsthand and secondhand account of the same event or topic; describe the differences in focus and the information provided.

standards.description: Interpret information presented visually, orally, or quantitatively and explain how the information contributes to an understanding of the text.
standards.ccssText: Interpret information presented visually, orally, or quantitatively (e.g., in charts, graphs, diagrams, time lines, animations, or interactive elements on Web pages) and explain how the information contributes to an understanding of the text in which it appears.

standards.description: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text.
standards.ccssText: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text.

standards.description: Integrate information from two texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably.
standards.ccssText: Integrate information from two texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably.

clusters.name: Range of reading and level of text complexity

standards.description: By end of year, read and comprehend informational texts in the grades 4-5 text complexity band proficiently.
standards.ccssText: By the end of year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, in the grades 4–5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

standards.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
standards.ccssText: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

subStandards.description: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.
subStandards.ccssText: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (e.g., roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.

standards.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
standards.ccssText: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

subStandards.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.
subStandards.ccssText: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

subStandards.description: Read on-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
subStandards.ccssText: Read on-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.

subStandards.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
subStandards.ccssText: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

standards.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information.
standards.ccssText: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information.

subStandards.description: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which related ideas are grouped to support the writer's purpose.
subStandards.ccssText: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which related ideas are grouped to support the writer's purpose.

subStandards.description: Provide reasons that are supported by facts and details.
subStandards.ccssText: Provide reasons that are supported by facts and details.

subStandards.description: Link opinion and reasons using words and phrases.
subStandards.ccssText: Link opinion and reasons using words and phrases (e.g., for instance, in order to, in addition).

subStandards.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.
subStandards.ccssText: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.

standards.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.
standards.ccssText: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

subStandards.description: Introduce a topic clearly and group related information in paragraphs and sections; include formatting, illustrations, and multimedia when useful.
subStandards.ccssText: Introduce a topic clearly and group related information in paragraphs and sections; include formatting (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

subStandards.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.
subStandards.ccssText: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.

subStandards.description: Link ideas within categories of information using words and phrases.
subStandards.ccssText: Link ideas within categories of information using words and phrases (e.g., another, for example, also, because).

subStandards.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.
subStandards.ccssText: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

subStandards.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented.
subStandards.ccssText: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented.

standards.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.
standards.ccssText: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

subStandards.description: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.
subStandards.ccssText: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

subStandards.description: Use dialogue and description to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.
subStandards.ccssText: Use dialogue and description to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.

subStandards.description: Use a variety of transitional words and phrases to manage the sequence of events.
subStandards.ccssText: Use a variety of transitional words and phrases to manage the sequence of events.

subStandards.description: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events precisely.
subStandards.ccssText: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events precisely.

subStandards.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.
subStandards.ccssText: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.

standards.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
standards.ccssText: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1–3 above.)

standards.description: With guidance and support, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.
standards.ccssText: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing. (Editing for conventions should demonstrate command of Language standards 1–3 up to and including grade 4 here.)

standards.description: With some guidance and support, use technology to produce and publish writing, and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient keyboarding skills.
standards.ccssText: With some guidance and support from adults, use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of one page in a single sitting.

clusters.name: Research to build and present knowledge

standards.description: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.
standards.ccssText: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.

standards.description: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; take notes and categorize information, and provide a list of sources.
standards.ccssText: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; take notes and categorize information, and provide a list of sources.

standards.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.
standards.ccssText: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

subStandards.description: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to literature.
subStandards.ccssText: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text [e.g., a character's thoughts, words, or actions].").

subStandards.skillName: Apply reading standards to informational text
subStandards.description: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to informational texts.
subStandards.ccssText: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to informational texts (e.g., "Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text").

standards.description: Write routinely over extended time frames and shorter time frames for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.
standards.ccssText: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

standards.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions with diverse partners on grade 4 topics and texts, building on others' ideas.
standards.ccssText: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 4 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

subStandards.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic.
subStandards.ccssText: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

subStandards.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.
subStandards.ccssText: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.

subStandards.description: Pose and respond to specific questions to clarify or follow up on information, and make comments that contribute to the discussion.
subStandards.ccssText: Pose and respond to specific questions to clarify or follow up on information, and make comments that contribute to the discussion and link to the remarks of others.

subStandards.description: Review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.
subStandards.ccssText: Review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

standards.description: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.
standards.ccssText: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

standards.description: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.
standards.ccssText: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.

standards.description: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using appropriate facts and relevant descriptive details to support main ideas or themes.
standards.ccssText: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace.

standards.description: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.
standards.ccssText: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.

standards.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English and situations where informal discourse is appropriate; use formal English when appropriate.
standards.ccssText: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion); use formal English when appropriate to task and situation.

standards.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.
standards.ccssText: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

subStandards.description: Use relative pronouns and relative adverbs.
subStandards.ccssText: Use relative pronouns (who, whose, whom, which, that) and relative adverbs (where, when, why).

subStandards.skillName: Form and use progressive verb tenses
subStandards.description: Form and use the progressive verb tenses.
subStandards.ccssText: Form and use the progressive (e.g., I was walking; I am walking; I will be walking) verb tenses.

subStandards.description: Use modal auxiliaries to convey various conditions.
subStandards.ccssText: Use modal auxiliaries (e.g., can, may, must) to convey various conditions.

subStandards.description: Order adjectives within sentences according to conventional patterns.
subStandards.ccssText: Order adjectives within sentences according to conventional patterns (e.g., a small red bag rather than a red small bag).

subStandards.description: Form and use prepositional phrases.
subStandards.ccssText: Form and use prepositional phrases.

subStandards.description: Produce complete sentences, recognizing and correcting inappropriate fragments and run-ons.
subStandards.ccssText: Produce complete sentences, recognizing and correcting inappropriate fragments and run-ons.

subStandards.description: Correctly use frequently confused words.
subStandards.ccssText: Correctly use frequently confused words (e.g., to, too, two; there, their).

standards.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
standards.ccssText: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

subStandards.description: Use correct capitalization.
subStandards.ccssText: Use correct capitalization.

subStandards.description: Use commas and quotation marks to mark direct speech and quotations from a text.
subStandards.ccssText: Use commas and quotation marks to mark direct speech and quotations from a text.

subStandards.description: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence.
subStandards.ccssText: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence.

subStandards.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.
subStandards.ccssText: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

standards.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.
standards.ccssText: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

subStandards.skillName: Choose words and phrases for effect
subStandards.description: Choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.
subStandards.ccssText: Choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.

subStandards.description: Choose punctuation for effect.
subStandards.ccssText: Choose punctuation for effect.

subStandards.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English and situations where informal discourse is appropriate.
subStandards.ccssText: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion).

standards.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 4 reading and content.
standards.ccssText: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 4 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

subStandards.description: Use context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
subStandards.ccssText: Use context (e.g., definitions, examples, or restatements in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

subStandards.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word.
subStandards.ccssText: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., telegraph, photograph, autograph).

subStandards.description: Consult reference materials to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.
subStandards.ccssText: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

standards.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.
standards.ccssText: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

subStandards.description: Explain the meaning of simple similes and metaphors in context.
subStandards.ccssText: Explain the meaning of simple similes and metaphors (e.g., as pretty as a picture) in context.

subStandards.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.
subStandards.ccssText: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

subStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of words by relating them to their opposites and to words with similar but not identical meanings.
subStandards.ccssText: Demonstrate understanding of words by relating them to their opposites (antonyms) and to words with similar but not identical meanings (synonyms).

standards.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases.
standards.ccssText: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal precise actions, emotions, or states of being (e.g., quizzed, whined, stammered) and that are basic to a particular topic (e.g., wildlife, conservation, and endangered when discussing animal preservation).
